Women’s Golf Wins Second Straight Tournament, Finishing First at the Blessings Collegiate Invitational

10/5/2026 6:02:00 PM | Women's Golf

Results
Share:
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:56
Instaread

Lydia Lasprilla becomes first head coach in program history to begin her tenure with two tournament victories

FAYETTEVILLE, Ark. – The Alabama women's golf team picked up its second consecutive tournament victory to start the 2026-27 season, taking home the team title at the Blessings Collegiate Invitational on Monday, finishing with a 54-hole score of 4-over par 868 (280-294-294).

For the second time in program history, the Crimson Tide has won its first two tournaments of the season, as the Tide was led by Manon Petitcolas (5-under par) and Amely Bochaton (3-under par), who each finished among the top five individuals.   

The Highlights

  • Alabama head coach Lydia Lasprilla became the first coach in program history to win her first two tournaments to begin their UA coaching tenure
  • Manon Petitcolas posted her second straight top-five finish to begin her collegiate career, finishing third overall at 5-under par 211 (69-72-70)
  • Amely Bochaton finished inside the top-10 for the second consecutive tournament to begin her UA career, placing fourth overall at 3-under par 213 (66-74-73)
  • In her first appearance in the UA lineup this season Alice Johansson cracked the top-10 with a 54-hole score of 6-over par 222 (72-74-76), finishing tied for ninth
  • Natachanok Tunwannarux finished in the top-10 for the third time during her UA career, ending the tournament at 6-over par 222 (73-74-75) placing ninth along with fellow teammate Johansson 
  • Tiphani Knight rounded out UA's lineup in a tie for 26th overall at 15-over par 231 (75-77-79)

Team Results

  • Alabama won the tournament by eight strokes with Arkansas finishing in second at 12-over par
  • Arkansas' Maria Jose Marin took home the individual crown at 12-under par

Up Next

  • Alabama will participate in the Haskins Intercollegiate from Oct. 12-13 in Columbus, Ga.
